title: What 214 meters underwater does to your lungs 🌊
subject: freediving
description:
How deep could you go on one breath? 👇

The diving reflex slows your heart the moment cold water hits your face, and at depth the pressure crushes your lungs. Herbert Nitsch went deeper than anyone, and the ascent was the hard part.

Sources: Wikipedia ("Herbert Nitsch", "Diving reflex", "Freediving", "No-limits apnea"), DeeperBlue ("Herbert Nitsch Talks About His Fateful Dive And Recovery"), Godek & Freeman, "Physiology, Diving Reflex", StatPearls (NIH NCBI)
tags: what happens to your body deep underwater
how deep can a human dive

scenes.text: Your heart slows when cold water hits your face.
Nerves around your nose and eyes trigger the diving reflex, saving oxygen for your brain.
Then the ocean squeezes. Every 10 meters adds one more atmosphere of pressure.
In 2007, Austrian Herbert Nitsch rode a sled to 214 meters. His lungs shrank to under a twentieth of their size.
Blood floods your chest to keep your lungs from collapsing.
In 2012, Nitsch hit 253 meters off Santorini. On the way up, he suffered several strokes.
